chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Stark's anger at Oxley over the drums
summary: Crawford says Herman Stark once told Oxley to take the band and leave, over the drums Crawford had paid for himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: He stood -- as he came through the door, came upstairs, he stood against the wall, over -- with his overcoat over his or either topcoat over his arm, dressed to kill, hair gleaming. Good looking man. And he just stood there, listened to the band. He didn't say anything or do anything, he and Herman Stocks. And so, (inaudible) well, he could make us or break us.
But one night Herman Stocks got so mad with Harold Oxley, he told him, take that band and get out of here. (Inaudible) squirmed.
What did he get mad at Oxley for?

Well, Oxley wanted some drums up there, wanted some drums up there which I bought and paid for myself out of my 60.00 or $65.00 a week. That was all that I was getting. I was mad at Lunsford about (inaudible).
Well now, you -- now, at that time the Cotton Club had --
They went on -- they were going to downtown, Paramount theaters and all the Loew's, State and all that. After weeks they put somebody in their place.
